item.title: Details emerge in case of former Cornell student alleging rape by frat members
item.description: A woman, identified only as Jane Doe, alleges she was gang-raped by seven fraternity members in 2024 and accuses Cornell University of failing to protect her.

item.title: Polo will impact the U.S. after slamming Mexico. See its path.
item.description: Former Hurricane Polo is expected to bring heavy rain and flooding to parts of the southwestern United States.

item.title: Attorney says there's "no evidence" Lindsay Clancy admitted killing her kids
item.description: In a surprising turn in Lindsay Clancy's first hearing since her mistrial in early September, her lawyer, Kevin Reddington, argued that there was no evidence she killed her kids.

item.title: Backpack voted Fat Bear Week 2026 winner, beating former champ's offspring
item.description: Voters were split between bear 910 and 89 Backpack in the final round of the weeklong contest to see who is the chunkiest bear at Katmai National Park and Preserve in Alaska.

item.title: Bureau of Prisons ordered to restore its union's contract
item.description: A federal judge on Tuesday ordered the Bureau of Prisons to reinstate a collective bargaining agreement with the agency's union after the bureau's director abruptly terminated it last year.

item.title: Hegseth directs military academies to stop giving tenure to civilian professors
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth ordered institutions like the Military Academy at West Point and the Naval Academy in Annapolis to stop granting tenure to civilian faculty, in his latest change to military higher education.

item.title: Iranian photojournalist facing 15 years in prison speaks out
item.description: Yalda Moaiery, an Iranian photojournalist who has spent her career documenting life in her home country, was sentenced to 15 years in prison in connection with her work. CBS News' Courtney Kealy has the details.

item.title: Cornell Jane Doe told campus police, "I can say with 100% confidence I was raped," transcript shows
item.description: The accuser in the alleged Cornell University gang rape told campus authorities she was "100%" sure she was raped just days after the incident, an interview transcript reviewed by CBS News New York shows. CBS News' Lilia Luciano has more.

item.title: Transcript shows campus police's interview with Jane Doe in Cornell rape case
item.description: We're getting new insight into how Cornell University Police handled the case of an alleged fraternity gang rape back in 2024.

item.title: Ethics expert on taxpayers paying for Trump's new ads
item.description: Christopher Swartz, former acting chief of ethics law at the U.S. Office of Government Ethics, joins "The Daily Report" to discuss the controversy over a series of new White House television ads paid for by taxpayers.

item.title: Former "American Idol" contestant Caleb Flynn found guilty in wife's murder
item.description: Flynn was found guilty of killing his wife, Ashley, in February and attempting to blame the murder on a break-in at their home.

item.title: Former "American Idol" contestant found guilty in wife's murder
item.description: Caleb Flynn, a former "American Idol" contestant and music pastor, was found guilty of murdering his wife. Ian Lee has details from the court.

item.title: After nor'easter strands wedding guests, local islanders show up to help couple tie the knot
item.description: After North Carolina got battered by the nor'easter last Friday, a couple had few guests who could make it to Hatteras Island for their wedding. So, they turned to social media to invite everyone on the island to celebrate.

item.title: The state of key races 35 days before midterms
item.description: A new poll from Marist shows Democrats leading the Senate and gubernatorial races in Ohio just 35 days before the midterms. CBS News' political director Fin Gómez breaks it down.

item.title: FAA investigates software glitch in some Boeing 737 Max jets
item.description: The FAA is investigating a software glitch in some Boeing 737 Max jets​ that could prompt an automated flight guidance system to disengage during an aborted landing.

item.title: Why Lindsay Clancy's attorney is only now questioning whether she committed killings
item.description: CBS News legal contributor Jessica Levinson breaks down why Lindsay Clancy's attorney might have decided now to question whether she committed the killings of her three children during a hearing on the timing of a potential new trial.

item.title: Winter holiday flight prices reach 10-year high in U.S. as Iran war sends fuel costs soaring
item.description: Winter holiday airfares reached a 10-year high in the U.S. amid Iran war price hikes, a new analysis by Hopper found. CBS News' Megan Cerullo has more.

item.title: Holiday flight costs hit highest level in a decade
item.description: Flying this holiday season will cost a whole lot more. Kris Van Cleave has details and how to save.

item.title: Video shows students saving their school bus, driver: "Our bus driver just passed out"
item.description: A school bus security camera caught quick-thinking students leaping into action after they noticed the bus driver limp over the steering wheel. Tom Hanson has the story.

item.title: Trump and Rubio question U.K. handling of possible plot against air base
item.description: Rubio claims a possible terror plot against a U.K. air base used by U.S. forces "clearly involved" a foreign actor, but there are few facts to support that.

item.title: Trump and major AI executives sign "morally binding" voluntary controls
item.description: President Trump and the leaders of the country's largest artificial intelligence companies have signed a set of voluntary safety standards, as calls mount for tighter guardrails on powerful AI technology.

item.title: Trump and tech leaders sign "morally-binding" AI "constitution" in safety push
item.description: President Trump met with key AI leaders at the White House on Tuesday, with the group signing what Mr. Trump called an AI "constitution" aimed at self-policing and safety. CBS News' Olivia Rinaldi has more.

item.title: 9/29: CBS Evening News
item.description: Life-threatening flood emergency in the Southwest; Jane Doe told Cornell police she was raped, CBS News New York reports.

item.title: 9/29: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: Trump and tech leaders sign AI "constitution" with voluntary controls; Jack Smith testifies before the Senate.

item.title: Sylvester Stallone on the fight to make "Rocky"
item.description: Sylvester Stallone was a struggling actor who wrote the perfect script for himself – and refused to sell it unless he played the title role. He talks about his new memoir, "The Steps," that recounts his rocky road to fame before and after "Rocky."

item.title: Raye on the big risk behind her biggest success
item.description: The British singer's songs have ranged in subject matter from being single to sexual assault and coping with drugs and alcohol. She talks about the risks and rewards of going it alone as an independent artist, and about her smash hit "Where Is My Husband!"

item.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang rejects AI extinction fear as "doomsday narratives"
item.description: Predictions that AI could destroy humanity in a few years are irresponsible and not based on science, Nvidia's co-founder told CBS News.

item.title: Charles Spencer on the royal fallout following Princess Diana's death
item.description: In his first interview about his new book, "Swan Song: Diana, My Sister," Charles Spencer talks about his attempt to set down what he calls the definitive story of Princess Diana.

item.title: Illustrating myths: The Lucas Museum of Narrative Art opens
item.description: The art of illustrators is at the core of a new L.A. institution founded by filmmaker George Lucas and businesswoman Mellody Hobson. They talk about the emotional pull of storytelling art and mythic narratives that shape our world.

item.title: Air Force officer prayed while "free-falling" after being shot down in Iran
item.description: Badly wounded and alone in Iran's desert, downed U.S. Air Force officer Dude 44 Bravo evaded capture for days as the Iranian forces and the U.S. military searched for him.
